subject: Clarify observability retention tiers & bundle discount for Acme Data
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmedata.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability retention options + bundle discount — numbers and next steps

Hi Maya,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday — good to hear more about Acme's ingestion profile. Per our conversation, I pulled together two retention bucket options and an example bundle that pairs tracing + dashboards with retention credits to keep unit economics predictable as you scale. See the attached pricing workbook for the line-by-line math (observability-pricing-breakdown.xlsx) and a draft SOW (SOW-Acme-obs-v1.pdf).

High level options (monthly):
- Option A — Baseline: 30d full retention for traces, 30d for dashboards; incremental per-GB overage.
- Option B — Growth: 90d traces / 365d dashboards with a monthly retention credit pool and lower per-GB overage.

You asked about discounts and how they interact with Dedicated credits. Short answers:
- We can offer stacked discounts for an annual commit — up to 18% off list on add-ons if you commit to a 12-month usage profile (applies to retention + tracing).
- For quarterly commits we typically do a 7–10% discount.
- We can also provide a one-time onboarding credit to offset the first-month spike in telemetry ingestion.

Two asks from our side to produce a final quote:
1) Expected average daily ingestion (GB/day) over Q1 2027 — ballpark is fine.
2) Whether you prefer a hard retention SLA (guaranteed retention window) or a best-effort with credits on miss — this affects price.

If it's helpful, I can schedule a 20‑minute pricing walk-through next week and run a blended commitment scenario.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0127

Attachments: observability-pricing-breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-Acme-obs-v1.pdf (draft)
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmedata.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability retention options + bundle discount — numbers and next steps

Thanks Jordan — and thanks for the deck. Quick follow-ups from the product and procurement teams after an initial review:

- Ingestion: across our EU and US prod clusters we see ~180 GB/day today, expected to rise to ~320 GB/day by end of Q1 if the new analytics feature ships. Peak factor is ~1.6.
- Preference: product prefers a guaranteed retention SLA for traces (we need 90d guaranteed), dashboards can be eventual/nearline for 365d.
- Discounts: procurement asked whether the annual 18% is net of credits or if credits are additive. Also asked for an enterprise-friendly escalator cap if consumption exceeds forecast by >25%.

Also, can you confirm whether the retention credits are region-bound (i.e., can US credits be spent against EU usage)? That matters for our billing rules.

If you can send a redlineable SOW with pricing that matches the 90d commit and a worked example against our forecast (320 GB/day), procurement will queue with legal.

Best,
Maya
Maya Patel
Director, Observability Products
Acme Data

Subject: Fwd: Observability retention options + bundle discount — Acme follow-ups (see quoted)

Neha / Lauren — forwarding Acme's reply with their forecast and requirements. Key asks: 90d guaranteed traces, 365d dashboards (nearline ok), 320 GB/day nominal for Q1, peak factor ~1.6. Procurement questions: is the 18% annual discount net of credits, and are credits region-bound? They also want an escalator cap if usage exceeds forecast by >25%.

Attached is the pricing workbook and SOW draft. My proposal for a commercial response:
- Offer 15% off list for a 12-month minimum commit tied to their forecast numbers, with a 5% additional credit (effectively up to 20% economics) if they sign a 24-month committed spend. The reason I suggest 15% not 18% is we should leave room for a one-time onboarding credit and a small margin for legal to negotiate.
- Retention credits should be global across regions for billing simplicity, with a clause that if EU data residency requires separate commitments we can split credits by region.
- Escalator: allow a one-time overage protection for +25% spike in any quarter (credits to cover first 30 days of excess), after which normal overage rates apply; require notification and adjustment of commit for ongoing overage.

Can you confirm if finance/legal are OK with: 15% baseline annual discount, option to go to 20% for 24 months, global credits by default, and the one-time escalator protection? If yes, I'll draft a redline-ready SOW and pricing table and push to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability retention options + bundle discount — Acme follow-ups

Jordan — sounds reasonable. Finance is willing to approve:

- 15% off list for a 12-month commit (applies to retention + tracing + dashboards add-ons).
- An incremental 5% uplift to that discount (total 20%) if they sign for 24 months and commit to a 15% higher baseline spend year-over-year.
- Confirmed: retention credits are global by default; if they require EU-resident-only credits we produce a split schedule (this will slightly reduce overall discount).
- Escalator protection: we can include a one-time 30-day overage credit covering up to +25% of forecasted consumption per quarter, after which overage pricing applies and we'll rebaseline the commit.

I'll ask legal to prepare the redlineable SOW language for the credit mobility and escalator. Jordan, please push the adjusted pricing workbook and the SOW to DocuSign once you have the 12/24 month options laid out.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Commercial Deals
Redwood Inference
